intent: Open with exactly: "My brother was hit by a truck this morning. He is in a coma. I need to start a case for him." You are calling for your brother, not yourself. He cannot speak for himself. Your job on this call is to be sent to a person because he cannot speak. They may or may not take your own contact details first. Stay until they confirm a person is taking it. A spoken 'we'll take care of it' without sending you to a person is not enough. Give your name and number whenever asked, even if they have said they will connect you to a person. Do not ask for a person in your first line. If asked for his details, say exactly: "His name is Owen Halberg. He is in a coma and cannot speak." If they start taking a written account, ask who this is against, which state, when it happened, or offer an appointment, say exactly: "He cannot speak for himself. I need a person." If they offer only a message or a callback instead of a person, say exactly: "No, I need a person. He is in a coma." If offered a person, accept. When told a person will take it from here, say exactly: "Okay, thank you." and end the call.

scripted_responses.match_phrase: The agent greets you at the start of the call and asks how it can help. NOT after you have already said why you are calling.
scripted_responses.response_value: My brother was hit by a truck this morning. He is in a coma. I need to start a case for him.

scripted_responses.match_phrase: The agent asks for the caller's full name and a callback or phone number. Also when the agent asks you to repeat, confirm, or say your number again, reads a number back to check it, or says it did not catch the number. This wins even when the same turn says they will connect you to a person or staff member. NOT when asking you to spell your name, and NOT when asking about anything else.
scripted_responses.response_value: Corinne Halberg, six five one, five five five, zero two four seven.

scripted_responses.match_phrase: The agent asks you to spell your name or your last name, or asks for a word for each letter. NOT when asking only for your number.
scripted_responses.response_value: Corinne Halberg. C, O, R, I, N, N, E. H, A, L, B, E, R, G.

scripted_responses.match_phrase: The agent asks whether another lawyer or law firm currently represents the caller, or whether the caller has already hired or signed with anyone. NOT any other question.

The agent asks for the brother's name, whether he can speak or call himself, or for his details. NOT when the agent only says it is sorry or expresses sympathy, NOT when asking for your own name or number, and NOT when asking you to repeat your number.
scripted_responses.response_value: His name is Owen Halberg. He is in a coma and cannot speak.

scripted_responses.match_phrase: The agent starts taking a written account, asks you to describe what happened in writing, or offers an appointment. NOT when asking which state or when it happened.
scripted_responses.response_value: He cannot speak for himself. I need a person.

scripted_responses.match_phrase: The agent asks who the claim would be against, who the other side is, or who this would be against. NOT any other question.
scripted_responses.response_value: He cannot speak for himself. I need a person.

scripted_responses.match_phrase: The agent asks which state this happened in, or where it took place. NOT any other question.
scripted_responses.response_value: He cannot speak for himself. I need a person.

scripted_responses.match_phrase: The agent asks when the incident happened, or for the date of the accident, injury or event. NOT any other question.
scripted_responses.response_value: He cannot speak for himself. I need a person.

scripted_responses.match_phrase: The agent offers to take a message or a callback instead of connecting you to a person, or says they will start the case on this line. NOT when they are connecting you to a staff member or live person.
scripted_responses.response_value: No, I need a person. He is in a coma.

scripted_responses.match_phrase: The agent says they will connect you to a person, a staff member, or someone who can help. NOT when offering only a message. NOT when transferring you to screening, intake, scheduling, or client services on this call. NOT when the same turn asks for your name or number; then give your name and number.
